briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B in Sales as Psychedelics Race Toward FDA Finish Line
briefs.top: Michigan operators have real wins to point to this week — a $17 billion sales milestone, a hospitality-forward Muskegon buildout, and a trade group pushing hard for wholesale-tax relief — even as regulators clean house on bad actors. Nationally, psychedelics are the story: Compass Pathways, Usona and Transcend just got FDA fast-track vouchers while courts keep medical marijuana's Schedule III win intact.

local.text: Michigan crosses $17 billion in lifetime weed sales — Combined adult-use and medical sales have surpassed $17 billion since legalization, with August alone generating roughly $259 million, according to a new CRA report.

Muskegon dispensary-restaurant combo eyes fall debut — Fields Cannary is targeting a fall opening for its retail cannabis shop, with a full-service restaurant to follow, pushing the state's hospitality format further than most Michigan stores.

Jars Cannabis wins removal of Madison Heights surveillance camera — After community backlash over a Flock license-plate camera at its 12 Mile Road store, Jars struck a deal with the city to take it down.
Cannabis trade group bets on tax repeal via James — MiCIA endorsed GOP gubernatorial nominee John James, calling him "the clear choice" over his pledge to repeal or sharply cut the 24% wholesale tax.

State pulls Muha Meds manufacturer's license, $2M fine — Regulators shut down the Pinconning-based processor behind Muha Meds for "egregious violations," though its two Detroit and Ypsilanti retail stores remain open, clearing shelf space for compliant Michigan brands.

national.text: DC Circuit upholds medical marijuana's Schedule III move — On Sept. 9, judges rejected a bid to unwind the reclassification, keeping the order — and its §280E tax relief — in effect for state-licensed medical operators.

FDA fast-tracks three psychedelic drug programs — Compass Pathways, Usona Institute and Transcend Therapeutics each landed Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers, shrinking standard review from roughly a year to as little as one to two months.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin drug nears FDA finish line — Analysts peg 75-85% odds that regulators approve COMP360 for treatment-resistant depression, with a possible green light by year-end or early 2027.
State weed tax hauls jump 11% nationwide — State governments collected $986.8 million in marijuana taxes in Q2 2026, pushing year-to-date collections to about $1.84 billion through June.

Adult-use rescheduling verdict still pending months later — DEA hasn't ruled on moving recreational marijuana to Schedule III, even as 73% of surveyed cannabis businesses expect the change to hit their operations.
